title: Sourdough Grilled Cheese (Cheddar + Gruyère)
description: Sharp cheddar for bite, Gruyère for stretch, fried inside a salty Parmesan crust.

steps.text: Grate the cheddar and Gruyère, toss them together, and let the pile sit out while you prep.
steps.why: Grated cheese melts evenly before the bread burns, and mixing means both cheeses in every bite. Room-temp cheese is the difference between a molten center and a cold one.

steps.text: Spread mayonnaise edge to edge on one face of each slice, then press the grated Parmesan onto the mayo so it sticks in an even layer.
steps.why: Mayo browns deeper and more evenly than butter, and it's the glue: the Parmesan fries into a frico shell, crisp and salty, where plain bread would just toast.

steps.text: Heat a skillet over medium-low (3-4 out of 10 on an aggressive pan) and melt the butter in it.
steps.why: Thick sourdough with this much cheese needs time, not heat. Too hot means a burnt crust over a cold core, and the Parmesan browns faster than plain bread.

steps.text: Lay 2 slices parm-side down, divide the cheese between them, cap with the other slices parm-side up. Cook 3 to 4 minutes, checking a corner at 3: the crust should be deep golden and lacy.
Flip, cover the pan with a lid, and cook 3 minutes more.
steps.why: The trapped heat melts the center fully while the second crust sets.

steps.text: Rest 1 minute on a rack or board, then cut on the diagonal.
steps.why: Straight from the pan the cheese runs out; one minute and it pulls instead.

notes.title: Watch the Parmesan
notes.body: The parm crust colors faster than buttered bread. If it's browning ahead of the melt, drop the heat rather than pulling early.

notes.title: Thick showpiece version
notes.body: For extra-thick slices, sear both sides on the stovetop, then finish 4 minutes in a 350°F oven. Crust stays put, core melts completely.

plating: Cut on the diagonal, stack the halves offset so the pull shows. Tomato soup alongside is the law.
elevations: Apple, the house option: 1/8-inch slices of Granny Smith or firm Honeycrisp, one single layer placed INSIDE between two layers of cheese, never against the bread. The melt anchors the slices and the fruit's moisture stays off the crust. Sweet-tart against the fat, old Wisconsin pairing.
A thin smear of Dijon on the inside faces: acid against all that richness. Apple or Dijon, not both - two acids argue.
Add 1 oz low-moisture mozzarella to the blend: it contributes nothing but stretch, which turns a good pull into a photo.

changelog.note: Created from chat. Parmesan crust adopted into the core recipe; apple slices added as the lead elevation rather than core.
